title: The popups that interrupt you
summary: Supermarket Simulator talks to you through popups of its own: the game keeps a manager, a set of kinds, questions and apologies, and information panels with their own content.
body: Popups are a system. The game runs them through a manager of its own rather than showing text wherever it happens to fit, which is why they behave consistently.
They come in kinds. The game sorts popups into types, so a question behaves differently from an apology rather than all messages looking the same.
Some of them wait. A popup can be raised after a delay rather than immediately, which is why the game can let a moment pass before it says anything.
They take focus. The game has a handler for popup focus, which is why a popup can take over input instead of being decoration you can ignore.
There are information panels. The game keeps information popups with their own elements and content records, so a longer explanation is assembled from parts rather than written out once.
One of them is about the grid. There is a canvas for grid system information, which is why the shop's layout can be explained in place rather than in a manual.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the information icon it draws on a popup, a blue i in a pale circle.
What this entry does not tell you: how many popups there are, when each is triggered, or whether they can be turned off. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Popups are run by a manager of their own.
The game sorts popups into types.
The build names its info button and info panel, and keeps a checkout warning of its own.
facts.evidence: asset names: Info Button, Info Panel, Checkout Warning SFX

facts.claim: There is a question popup and an apology popup.
A popup can take focus over input.
There are information popups assembled from their own elements and content.
One popup covers grid system information.
A second manager runs popups independently of the first, with pieces of its own.
Information popups have a manager and kinds of their own.
A popup can ask for a confirmation through a handler of its own.
The game also keeps a stream of player notifications, placed by position.
The game draws an information icon of its own for a popup.
